title: Magneto-optical response and luminescence properties of lanthanide–titanium–oxo clusters Eu2Ti7 and Sm2Ti7

synthesis.procedure: Lanthanum acetate hydrate, titanium(IV) isopropoxide and 3,5-di-tert-butylbenzoic acid were dissolved in ethanol by sonication in sealed vials and reacted solvothermally at 80 °C for 24–48 h. Colorless block crystals were obtained without cooling to room temperature. The main text gives no numerical reagent amount, concentration or stoichiometric equivalent.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Sonication followed by solvothermal reaction in sealed vials
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Colorless block crystals obtained without cooling to room temperature
synthesis.yield: Over 40%, based on lanthanum acetate hydrate

source_locations.location: Synthesis, Structure and Characteristic; Synthesis scheme, La2Ti7

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The triclinic P-1 molecular cluster has a [La2Ti7(μ3-O)6]22+ core with two eight-coordinate La(III) and seven six-coordinate Ti(IV) ions, stabilized by 14 carboxylate and eight ethoxide ligands. The article describes it as two [LaTi4(μ3-O)3] units sharing one Ti(IV) ion in a hand-in-hand arrangement.

properties.summary: Orange-red Sm(III) luminescence is weaker and shorter-lived than that of the Eu analogue. Weak emission prevented reliable MCPL analysis, but near-infrared absorption enabled magnetic circular dichroism under an applied field.

properties.summary: The Eu cluster gives intense red luminescence with higher quantum yields and a longer lifetime than the Sm analogue. Its achiral solution exhibits magnetic circularly polarized luminescence under a 1.6 T field, but no CPL signal without the field.

synthesis.procedure: A dichloromethane solution of Eu2Ti7 was allowed to evaporate, producing colorless block crystals of a different crystalline phase. The article does not specify a numerical preparation quantity for this recrystallization.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Colorless block crystals formed on evaporation

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: SCXRD identified the recrystallized material as Eu2Ti7, but with triclinic P-1 symmetry instead of the original monoclinic C2/c symmetry. The authors suggest that dichloromethane molecules incorporated into the lattice may account for the change; their number is not established in the main text.
